1

 Judgment

Unfortunate tale of minor child Vishnu, aged about 9 years, who met with an accident, suffered amputation of right leg, approached this Court in this appeal aggrieved by judgment and award dated 26.09.2017 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Sedam (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' for brevity) in MVC No.1254/2015.

The appellant, minor child Vishnu, represented by his mother and natural guardian, is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground that the Tribunal has awarded meager and inadequate compensation.

2. Young and energetic minor child Vishnu, aged about 9 years, who was returning from his school on 19.09.2015 at about 11.00am, unmindful of the fact and consequences that would occur on the said date and time which would turn around his life up side down and create an unexpected vaccume in remaining part of his life.

While crossing the road to go to his house and immediately to play with his parents and his peer group, at that time APSRTC bus bearing Registration No.AP-11 /
Z-5788 came from VCF factory driven by the driver of the bus in a high speed and rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety, without consideration of life and consequences of the minor child Vishnu, who was crossing the road after alighting from the school bus, dashed against him.
3. Due to the said impact, minor child Vishnu fell down on the road and bus ran over the right thigh of the minor child Vishnu, wherein minor child Vishnu sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sedam.
On initial diagnosis the Doctor advised that the minor child Vishnu be shifted for better and higher treatment to any other hospital.
Accordingly, they shifted the minor child Vishnu to Kamareddy Hospital, Kalaburagi.
Pursuant to the accident a criminal case came to be registered in Cr. No. 229/2015 before the Sedam Police Station against the driver of offending bus.

4. It is an unfortunate tale of the mother of the minor child Vishnu, who represents him as natural guardian, that the minor child Vishnu was absolutely hale and healthy prior to the accident and most cheerful boy with enormous energy and world ahead of him to be conquered, has lost his entire right leg due to the rash and negligent manner of driving and inhuman act of the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation.
The unfortunate mother unable to bear the trauma herself and that of the minor child Vishnu filed a claim petition seeking compensation from the respondent - Corporation.

5. On issuance of notice to the respondent - Corporation, objection statement came to be filed, inter alia, denying the averments made in the claim petition and pleaded that it was the fault of the minor child Vishnu himself, who crossed the road without taking due care by looking left and right of the road and ran across and thereby got himself injured in a busy road and it is not a rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation.

It is also pleaded by the respondent - Corporation that though the minor child Vishnu has lost his right limb, he is only entitled to compensation as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/
2 LIMITED AND OTHERS, reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further pleaded that the minor child Vishnu would not be entitled to exorbitant compensation sought for by the mother in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the same.
6. On the basis of the pleadings the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the mother of the minor child Vishnu examined herself as PW1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P13.
She also examined the Doctor as PW2.
On the other hand, the respondent - Corporation examined its Manager as RW1, but no documents were marked on their behalf.

8. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the tribunal awarded the compensation in a sum of Rs. 7,00,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum and directed the respondent to pay the compensation.
9. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded, claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

10. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant-claimant - minor child Vishnu,
represented by his mother and natural guardian that the Tribunal has erred in awarding meager compensation and has not taken into consideration the material evidence both oral and documentary thereby causing miscarriage of justice to the claimant.

He further contends that the Tribunal has not at all applied its mind in awarding compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case wherein the minor child Vishnu, loaded with energy and enthusiasm, has lost his right leg due to the rash and negligent manner of driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation.

11. Learned Counsel for appellant - claimant further submits that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing proper income for arriving at calculation for assessing future income and has awarded global compensation of Rs.5,000/- per month towards loss of future income in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUNA, stated supra.
He further disagrees with the finding and calculation arrived at by the Tribunal and seeks enhancement of compensation.

12. Learned Counsel for appellant - claimant further contends that the Tribunal has lost sight of the facts and circumstances of the present case and has failed to award compensation under the head loss of marriage prospects; compensation towards future medical expenses; just and reasonable compensation under pain and suffering and compensation under the head attendant charges for the remaining part of the life of the appellant - claimant.
13. Learned Counsel for the appellant - claimant further contends that the Tribunal has committed serious error in not adding future prospects towards loss of future earning.
On all these ground he contends that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation commensurate to the injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu.
On these grounds he seeks to allow this appeal and enhance the compensation in a reasonable manner.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Counsel Sri Deshmuk appearing on behalf of respondent - Corporation vehemently contends that the judgment and award of the Tribunal is just and reasonable and the Tribunal has considered all the material evidence both oral and documentary and has kept in mind magnitude of the injuries suffered by the minor child Vishnu and has taken all precautions and care while awarding just and reasonable compensation for the injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu.
16. Learned Counsel for the respondent - Corporation further contends that the Tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation under other heads, which does not call for interference.

He further contends that the Tribunal has properly considered the disability at 85% based on the evidence adduced by PW2 - Doctor to the whole body and has accordingly granted suitable compensation in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUNA,
stated supra.

Learned Counsel sustains the order of the Tribunal by contending that the Tribunal has not lost sight of the fact that minor child Vishnu has lost his right leg and his entire life is ruined because of accident.
However, He further contends that the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation as a solace to the minor child Vishnu and his parents.
On these grounds he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the appellant - claimant.

17. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent - Corporation, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation, which calls for interference by this Court?
ii) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
iii) What order 18.

It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 19.09.2015 around 11.00 a.m. when the minor child Vishnu was crossing the road after attending his school to go to his house, during which time the offending bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation dashed against him leading to unfortunate incident of accident due to which his right leg was amputated.

19. In order to establish this fact of occurrence of accident, involvement of the vehicle belonging to respondent - Corporation and the same having occurred in a road traffic accident in a public place,
PW1, who is none other than the unfortunate mother, has deposed by producing Ex.P1 to P6, which are Police records, being FIR, charge sheet, crime details form, wound certificate and copy of the MVA report.
These documents exhibited after the investigation conducted by the jurisdictional Police, are not seriously disputed and there is no challenge to the same.

There being no challenge to these police records and laying of the charge sheet by the jurisdictional police, which is proved by Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/
4 the claimant that the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation was involved in the accident,
dashed against the minor child Vishnu, due to which he has suffered amputation of his right leg.
Hence, it will not detain this Court much longer to decide the aspect of occurrence of accident,
involvement of vehicle and injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu due to the rash and negligent manner of driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation.
20. Now, coming to the next aspect of what should be the compensation?

In the present case on hand, admittedly, injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu, who is about 9 years old when returning to his house after attending the school, unmindful of the consequences that would occur on the said date and time, in his normal playful manner and as any normal child would foresee remaining part of the day to spend playing with his parents and peer group, crossed the road.
In the meanwhile, the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation dashed against him leading to the accident and amputation of right leg of the minor child Vishnu.

21. In such cases, where the minor child is involved in accident and get injured, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in the case of MALLIKARJUNA, stated supra, so also, in the case of KAJAL, stated supra, as to how the Tribunal and this Court will have to deal with the matter.

22. It is no mere res-integra that in the case where the minor children are involved in a road traffic accident, the issue of income and computation of compensation has to be made in the manner prescribed in the aforesaid two cases.
But, however, it is not a stright jacket formula; as each and every case will have to be dealt under the facts and circumstances of such case.

23. In the present case on hand, the appellant has got examined the Doctor as PW2, who has deposed before the Court by adducing his evidence and stated that the minor child Vishnu has undergone amputation of the right leg and has suffered permanent physical disability assessed at 85% towards lower limb and 85% to the whole body.

I have perused the original records produced at Ex.P1 to P13, more specifically, disability certificate at Ex.P9 and photograph of the minor child Vishnu, post amputation of right leg at Ex.P10 and P11
, there is no iota of doubt in my mind that entire right leg has been amputated above thigh.
This will have to be kept in mind while this Court decides the compensation that would have to be awarded to the minor child Vishnu.

24. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal stated supra which was decided in the year 2020, the Hon'ble Apex Court has taken the minimum wages payable to a workmen as the basis of assessment of income for award of compensation.
The Karnataka State Legal Services Committee has prescribed the income chart to arrive at standard assessment of income in cases where there is no proof of income produced by the claimant.

25. I am of the opinion that instead of adverting into Minimum Wages Act, it would be appropriate in the facts and circumstance of the case to rely upon the Legal Services Committee chart wherein the notional income is prescribed for the relevant year of accident.
As per the notional income chart for the accident of the year 2015, the income is prescribed at Rs.8,000/- per month.

Accordingly,
the income in the present case has to be assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month rather than taking notional income at Rs.15,000/- per annum as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/

26. I am in agreement with the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant that the tribunal has lost sight of not applying future prospects in the present case on hand and failed to award additional amount towards future prospects.

Therefore, an addition of 40% towards the income stated above would have to be awarded towards loss of future earning capacity as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others,
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

In a case on hand, where the minor child is involved in the road traffic accident the appropriate multiplier that would be applicable is 18 and in the present case the multiplier is taken at 18 as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: The tribunal has failed to take into consideration this aspect of awarding compensation and adding future prospects and has awarded the global compensation on the basis of the case of Mallikarjun stated supra.
I do not agree the said finding of the tribunal.

The evidence of PW.2 the doctor is apparently unambiguous and not contraoverted by the respondent- Corporation to the effect that there is an amputation of entire right leg and there is a disability of 85% to the whole body.
Considering this aspect, the tribunal has totally failed in its application of mind to grant compensation under the head present and future attendant charges.

Admittedly and evidently based on the material evidence on record, it is seen that the minor child Vishnu has lost his right leg fully he would require the assistance of another person one attendant would be required to help and assist the minor child till his remaining part of the life as the entire right leg has been amputated.

In order to decide this aspect of attendant charges for the remaining part of the life, I am of the opinion that the notional income chart having been prescribed, the income of Rs.8,000/- could be taken at 50% for an attendant as income.

Therefore, under the head loss of future attendant charges would be:
Rs.8,64,000/- (Rs.4,000 x 12 x 18).
30. The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head pain and suffering.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellant- claimant that the said amount is extremely on the lower side.

Considering the fact that the minor child has suffered amputation of right leg and was admitted to the hospital for a period of 23 days having undergone enormous amount of pain,
agony and trauma, which cannot be compensated by way of cost, but the only factor which this Court can consider is what is the amount that can be act as solace to the minor child as well as to the parents.
In the present case since the minor child has incurred 85% disability, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- under this head as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

sentences.text: Towards medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded Rs.1,53,500/- which is on the basis of actual medical bills produced at Ex.P13, I do not find any reasons to interfere with the same.

Hence,
it is retained.
32. Towards attendant, food and conveyance charges during the period of treatment, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.11,500/- which is on the lower side.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under this head as against Rs.11,500/- awarded by the tribunal.
33. The tribunal has failed to take into consideration the loss of future prospects and marriage prospects for the minor child as his right leg is amputated.
The chances of marriage and enjoyment of sexual pleasure which is part of human life becomes extremely rare.

Hence, under this head, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.3 Lakhs.
34.
The tribunal has failed to award any compensation towards future medical expenses.

In the present case on hand, the injured minor child having sustained 85% disability to the whole body due to amputation of the right leg, which would be extremely difficult for the minor child for his mobility and movement in and around the house without the help of crutches and an artificial leg may make him mentally and physically dependant on himself.

It is also necessary to see that there may be several other expenditures which the minor child may incur in future for which he cannot be forced to come to this Court or there may not be an option to approach this Court seeking additional compensation for the future medical treatment, which would be incurred by the claimant.

Hence,
this Court would have to award suitable and reasonable future medical expenses.
This analysis is fortified in the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal stated supra.

No doubt, the opinion of the doctor is with regard to the permanent physical disability to an extent of 85% to the whole body of the minor child who has suffered physical disability of amputation of the entire right leg.
But the fact remains that due to the amputation of the entire right leg, there is a sever dent and blow to the psyche and the psychological balance of the minor child.
Hence, undoubtedly there would be certain amount of mental, pain and agony as well.
Hence, under this head, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- (five lakhs).
35. Towards loss of amenities, nutrition food, the tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- which again is on the extremely lower side.

Considering the fact that the minor child has lost his right leg, the loss of love and affection, pain and agony undergone by the minor child as well as the parents, the reasonable amount would be awarded towards loss of amenities.
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1 Lakh under this head.

36. In view of the above discussions, the appellant-claimant would be entitled to compensation as mentioned in the table below;
